record.original_question: For semigroup elements a and b, define a ∼p b to mean that there exist u and v in the semigroup with a = uv and b = vu. If a semigroup embeds into a group, must this relation ∼p be transitive on that semigroup?

evidence.quote: Since free semigroups are embeddable in groups, Problem 6.4 asks whether ∼p is transitive for any semigroup that can be embedded in a group.
Corollary 5.2. There exists a semigroup that is embeddable in a group for which ∼p is not transitive.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $S$ be a semigroup. Define a binary relation $\sim_p$ on $S$ by declaring $a \sim_p b$ if and only if there exist elements $u, v \in S$ such that $a = uv$ and $b = vu$. Suppose that $S$ embeds (as a semigroup) into some group. Must the relation $\sim_p$ be transitive on $S$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is answered in the negative: there exists a semigroup embeddable in a group on which the relation $\sim_p$ fails to be transitive. This resolves the problem (originally posed as Problem 6.4 in the Araújo–Kinyon–Konieczny–Malheiro list of open problems on semigroup conjugacy), with the counterexample provided as a corollary in recent work answering several such open problems.

status_evidence.title: Answering Four Open Problems Involving Semigroup Conjugacy (CMUP)
status_evidence.snippet: Talk announcement describing the resolution of four open problems on semigroup conjugacy, including the question of whether p-conjugacy is transitive on group-embeddable semigroups.
status_evidence.claim: The transitivity question for ∼p on group-embeddable semigroups has been resolved (negatively) in recent work answering four open problems on semigroup conjugacy.

status_evidence.title: On three approaches to conjugacy in semigroups
status_evidence.snippet: Background reference on the notion ∼p of p-conjugacy in semigroups and its transitivity properties.
status_evidence.claim: The relation ∼p (a = uv, b = vu) is a standard notion of conjugacy for semigroups whose transitivity is known to fail in general.
